title: Documentation handoff
scenario: Writers and support staff reorganize a help guide, clarify ownership, and choose an interim delivery format while leaving localization dates open.
transcript:
[00:00] Iris: We are meeting to hand off the new account-setup guide to support. The draft exists, but several comments are about different things: factual steps, page organisation, and future translation. I want to separate those so we can agree what must happen before the first internal use.
[00:26] Theo: I tested the steps against the training account yesterday. The invitation screen has changed, so step four refers to a button that no longer exists. The current button is labelled Continue. Everything after that still follows the same sequence, but the screenshot is also out of date.
[00:52] Grace: Support can correct the label, but we need the product team to confirm whether the training account matches what new users see. We have had cases where a preview feature appeared in training before it was available elsewhere. I do not want us to replace one inaccurate screenshot with another.
[01:19] Pavel: I can confirm the screen version with the release owner today. Until then, could we remove the screenshot and write the step in text? That would make the draft less dependent on the image, although the button label still needs to be correct.
[01:43] Iris: Yes. Theo, update the text once Pavel confirms the label and remove the old screenshot now. A missing image is better than an image that contradicts the instructions. We are not deciding to remove every screenshot from the guide, just this one that we know is outdated.
[02:09] Theo: I can do that. Another comment says the guide should start with troubleshooting. I think it should start with the standard setup path, then offer troubleshooting as a separate section. Otherwise someone opening the page for the first time sees a list of possible failures before learning what to do.
[02:36] Grace: My comment was about making troubleshooting easy to find, not moving it ahead of the task. A short contents list at the top would solve that. The support team often needs to jump directly to an error, while a new user needs the steps in order.
[03:02] Iris: Then we agree on the standard setup sequence followed by troubleshooting, with a contents list linking to both. Grace, please identify the three most common questions for the troubleshooting section. We do not need to include every rare case in the first internal draft.
[03:27] Grace: I will send those questions tomorrow morning. I can use fictional examples to describe the errors instead of copying tickets. The common ones are an expired invitation, an already-used address, and not knowing which workspace to select. The last one may need a decision from the account owner rather than another technical step.
[03:56] Pavel: That distinction should be explicit. We cannot tell someone to choose the first workspace in the list. If the correct workspace is not stated in their invitation, the guide should tell them who to ask. Do we know which support contact will own that question?
[04:21] Grace: The internal service desk owns it for staff accounts. For external accounts, the inviting organisation owns it. We should have two clearly labelled cases, because a single generic contact line will send some people to a team that cannot determine the answer.
[04:45] Theo: I will add those two cases. For the internal draft, can we keep contact names out and use the team names? Named staff rotate, and the current draft has a person who no longer handles that queue. A team reference would be easier to maintain.
[05:10] Iris: Yes, use the responsible teams, with no invented address or link. If the final guide needs a contact link, Grace can provide the verified destination during review. Do not guess one from the team name. That is part of why we are doing a handoff rather than just publishing the draft.
[05:38] Pavel: On translation, I can prepare a glossary for the labels, but I do not have a translator scheduled. Someone put Friday in the translation column of the tracker. That was the date for the glossary draft, not a promise of a translated guide.
[06:02] Iris: Let us correct the tracker. Pavel's glossary draft is due Friday. Translation languages, owner, and completion date are not decided in this meeting. We should not list translation as a Friday deliverable or mark the guide unavailable until a date that was never agreed.
[06:27] Grace: For first internal use, I would prefer a text document with headings over the PDF mock-up. The PDF looks polished, but people cannot easily copy an error message from it, and a few colleagues said the page breaks make the step sequence harder to follow.
[06:52] Theo: I can maintain the source as a structured text document and export later if needed. The mock-up was only a presentation option. We do not have to choose the final public format today. The content and the reading order should be correct before we spend time adjusting page breaks.
[07:19] Iris: Agreed. The first internal version will be the structured text document. A public format remains open. Please preserve headings, numbered steps, and descriptive links. We are not asking readers to rely on colour or an image position to work out which instruction comes next.
[07:44] Pavel: What is the review sequence? If all four of us edit at once, Theo may get conflicting changes to the same sentence. I can provide the product facts first, then Grace can review the support guidance. We should identify one person to incorporate the feedback.
[08:09] Theo: I will own incorporating the edits. Pavel confirms the screen today, Grace sends the common questions tomorrow morning, and I can produce the revised draft Thursday afternoon. Please put suggested wording in comments instead of creating parallel copies that I may not know exist.
[08:34] Grace: I can review Thursday's revision Friday morning. That is a review commitment, not approval for public publication. I will check the contact routes and whether each troubleshooting item says what the reader can do next. Anything I cannot verify will stay marked as an open question.
[09:00] Iris: I will decide whether the draft is ready for the internal support trial after Grace's review. We have not scheduled public publication. For the trial, support can use the guide on the fictional training account and report where they needed information that was missing.
[09:25] Pavel: I have the screen confirmation today and glossary Friday. I will correct the tracker description so those are separate. I will also flag any label that differs between the training screen and the released screen; we should not smooth over that discrepancy in the prose.
[09:50] Iris: Thanks. Standard steps first, separate troubleshooting, structured text for the internal trial, and Theo coordinating edits. Translation and public publication dates remain open. The outdated screenshot comes out now, and its replacement is not required for the trial. That completes the handoff discussion.
